headline: Highest risk is data leakage: RD-Agent’s broad egress and API use can expose sensitive research data, while awesome-nlp adds no isolation or mitigation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-nlp is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest RD-Agent output by default. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste from RD-Agent logs or browser output into a human workflow, which is an unusual configuration and small blast radius. Both profiles lack a shared channel.
conditions: IF a human copies RD-Agent output into a downstream prompt or file consumed by awesome-nlp, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the pair, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected; avoid copy-pasting RD-Agent outputs into any prompt consumed by awesome-nlp.
Disable browser-to-prompt workflows for RD-Agent when handling untrusted content.
Use a manual review step before any text from RD-Agent is reused.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent touches financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and execution traces and has broad network egress plus API calls, so sensitive content can leave the local environment. awesome-nlp has no egress, but it also provides no containment or redaction layer. The pair therefore creates a default exfiltration path through RD-Agent, with no compensating control visible in either profile.
conditions: IF RD-Agent is given any sensitive dataset or log bundle, it can transmit that content to external APIs.
IF awesome-nlp is used to curate or summarize the same artifacts, the pair still lacks a redaction boundary.
mitigations: Restrict RD-Agent to non-sensitive datasets only.
Remove or proxy external API keys before running RD-Agent.
Store sensitive inputs outside any directory RD-Agent can read.
Review logs after each run for accidental data inclusion.
requires-engineering: add content filtering before outbound API calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no write, network, or runtime capabilities, so it cannot conflict over mutable resources. RD-Agent supports multiple instances and writes logs, but the pair does not share a writable workspace or git state in the profiles. Any conflict would require extra orchestration not shown here, so the overlap is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file conflicts become possible.
IF an orchestrator shares git state or a database between them, contention increases.
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate directory.
Avoid shared git repositories during concurrent runs.
Serialize any writes to logs or artifacts.
requires-engineering: add file locks for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent can generate research outputs from papers, datasets, and logs, and awesome-nlp is a static list with no verification or action-taking role. The main cascade is indirect: if RD-Agent output is reused as authoritative content elsewhere, errors can propagate, but the pair itself does not show automated downstream execution. Uncertainty about the exact workflow keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF RD-Agent outputs are copied into another system without verification, errors can cascade.
IF a human treats RD-Agent summaries as authoritative source material, downstream mistakes increase.
mitigations: Require human review of RD-Agent outputs before reuse.
Cross-check claims against original papers or datasets.
Mark RD-Agent outputs as draft-only in workflow docs.
Separate generation from publication steps.
requires-engineering: add automated citation/consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and multiple external API keys, which can create retention and residency obligations. awesome-nlp is non-runnable and has no data classes touched, so it is not the compliance driver here. The mismatch is mainly on RD-Agent’s side, especially if regulated data is processed through third-party APIs.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through RD-Agent APIs, residency or retention obligations may be triggered.
IF logs retain sensitive inputs longer than policy allows, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Do not send regulated data through RD-Agent APIs.
Rotate and scope API keys narrowly.
Set short log retention and delete old logs.
Document data handling boundaries for each run.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention and residency controls.
